title: History retention is count-only — 30 full transcripts can mean unbounded disk with no age or size policy
existing_state: Main execution history retention is purely count-based: EnforceRetention trims the index to MaxHistoryEntries and deletes evicted run files (Services/HistoryStorageService.cs:674-683, invoked from SaveRun at :474). MaxHistoryEntries defaults to 30 (Models/AppConfiguration.cs:73) and the Settings dialog exposes only that single number, clamped 1-500 (SettingsDialog.cs:2550, 2667). Each run payload stores the full combined output plus per-host outputs plus ExecutionDetails including interactive-terminal transcripts, so a 200-host run file can be tens of megabytes; 500 of them is multi-GB with no age-based pruning and no visibility into usage. Notably the scheduler's job history DOES have day-based retention (DefaultHistoryRetentionDays, AppConfiguration.cs:152) — main history is the odd one out.
recommendation: Add optional age-based retention ("delete runs older than N days", mirroring the existing job-history policy) and an optional total-size cap to EnforceRetention; surface both next to the Max History numeric in SettingsDialog along with a live "History is using 412 MB (37 runs)" readout computed from the run folder, with a 'Clean up now' button.
user_benefit: A daily 200-host operator either keeps history tiny (losing the audit trail) or lets multi-GB run files accumulate invisibly in %LocalAppData%. Age/size policies plus a usage readout match what the app already does for scheduled-job history.

evidence.note: MaxHistoryEntries default 30; no age/size knobs for main history
only the count is exposed in settings
